name: IL-13
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by about five points on the partisan baseline
Incumbent Nikki Budzinski has a massive financial edge: $2.6M on hand versus roughly $12K for Jeff Wilson
Prediction markets price her near 96% to win
No public general-election polling, so the forecast rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: Budzinski combines a favorable district lean, incumbency, and an overwhelming fundraising advantage, while markets price her near-certain to win. With no polls or expert ratings to move the estimate, the forecast stays close to the fundamentals-based margin.
model.watch: A late surge of outside Republican spending or an unexpectedly strong national GOP environment could narrow the margin, though a seat flip remains unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
First-term incumbent Nikki Budzinski seeks reelection in an Illinois district that leans Democratic by about five points. She has raised nearly $2.9 million and holds $2.6 million on hand, while Republican challenger Jeff Wilson has raised about $348,000 with only $12,000 remaining. No outside groups have meaningfully engaged on either side, and no public general-election polling is available.

Prediction markets give Budzinski roughly a 96% chance of winning, and no expert raters list the race as competitive. The fundamentals point to a comfortable incumbent win in the mid-to-high teens, with the main uncertainty coming from the absence of polling rather than any specific sign of vulnerability.
